newsitem.title: USA: Government terms behavior of many U.S. teens risky.
newsitem.headline: Government terms behavior of many U.S. teens risky.

text.p: A government risk survey found that nearly 9 percent of high school students had attempted suicide, while one-fourth had smoked marijuana and half had drunk alcohol in the previous month, officials said Thursday.

A wide-ranging 1995 survey of 10,904 students by the U.S. Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) also found that many youths were sexually active without using condoms. Others rode with drunk drivers, smoked cigarettes or ate too much fat.

"Too many high school students nationwide are practicing behaviours that place them unnecessarily at risk for serious health, education and social problems, both today and in the future," said Dr. Laura Kann, chief of surveillance research in the CDC's Division of Adolescent and School Health.

The survey found that 39 percent of the students had ridden in the past month with a driver who had been drinking alcohol. "Motor vehicle crashes are the leading cause of death among kids," Kann said. "These kids have put themselves in a situation that might contribute to a motor vehicle crash."

The survey found that 8.8 percent of the adolescents had attempted suicide in the past year. And in the month before the survey, 20 percent had carried a weapon, 25 percent had used marijuana, 35 percent had smoked cigarettes and 52 percent had had at least one alcoholic drink.
It also found that 40 percent had eaten more than two servings of high-fat foods on the day before the survey.

About 40 percent of the students in grades 9 through 12 also said they had had sexual intercourse in the past three months. Of those, 46 percent said they did not use a condom. Nearly 18 percent said they had already had sexual intercourse with at least four people during their lifetimes.

Kann said that compared to surveys taken in the early 1990s, tobacco, marijuana and cocaine use had increased, while alcohol use was unchanged. The rate of suicide attempts by high school students declined in the past few years, while seatbelt and condom use increased, she said.

"The percent of students who have had sexual intercourse, the percent who have had multiple partners and the percent who've had sexual intercourse in the past three months has not changed," Kann said.
Despite the improvements in some areas, "there are still too many kids practicing these behaviours that unnecessarily will place them at risk for health, education and social problems," she said.
